misconceptions.description: Treating a right or wrong verdict as instructional feedback rather than information the learner can act on
misconceptions.trigger: learner designs a check that only says Correct or Incorrect with a score and no path to improve
misconceptions.feedback: Feedback must be actionable. Beyond a verdict, tell the learner what was misunderstood and what to try next, or the loop teaches nothing.

misconceptions.description: Equating learner control with unlimited freedom to skip, reorder, or exit, ignoring that novices often choose poorly
misconceptions.trigger: learner gives full skip-everything control to beginners who lack the prior knowledge to self-regulate
misconceptions.feedback: Learner control should be calibrated to expertise. Offer guided control (recommended path plus optional detours) for novices rather than unbounded freedom.

misconceptions.description: Assuming immediate feedback is always superior, even when delayed feedback would better support retention or transfer
misconceptions.trigger: learner attaches instant answer reveals to tasks meant to build retrieval or self-monitoring
misconceptions.feedback: Feedback timing is a design choice. For tasks that build retrieval or self-assessment, brief delay can strengthen learning more than instant reveal.
